title: observability: token-level KV cache tracing, cost/latency dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Ava Chen
description: Adds token-level KV cache tracing and integrates token-level cost/latency breakdowns into dashboards with tuned alerting thresholds. Motivation: recent incidents and bench runs showed KV cache misses and token-level latency spikes contributing to tail latency and cost overruns for long-context workloads. This PR introduces: 1) structured tracing for KV cache lookups with trace IDs and sampleable spans; 2) new Prometheus metrics and OTLP export for token_cache.{hit,miss,lookup_time_ms} with cardinality controls; 3) a Grafana dashboard for token-level cost/latency and KV hit-rate visualizations; 4) alert tuning (P95/P99 latency and KV miss-rate) with runbook links and automatic paging suppression for expected transient spikes. Includes small performance guardrails (metric tags, sample rate, aggregation windows) to keep telemetry cost bounded. Checklist: [x] new tracing proto/messages and exporter; [x] metric instrumentation and aggregation rules; [x] dashboard panels and annotations; [x] alert rules and runbook; [x] unit + integration tests; [x] load/perf verification. Related: ENG-592, ENG-605, SUP-2431.
commit_summary: feat(observability): add token-level KV cache tracing proto and exporter
feat(metrics): instrument token_cache.hit/miss/lookup_time_ms and aggregation rules
feat(dashboards): add token-level cost/latency + KV hit-rate Grafana dashboard
chore(alerts): tune p95/p99 latency alerts and add runbook links
test: add unit and integration tests for new telemetry paths
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Left a few suggestions on aggregation windows - P99 on 1s bins looks noisy in canary; recommend 10s for production. See inline.
Ava Chen: Agreed, adjusted aggregation to 10s for P99 and kept a 1s sampling window for high-fidelity debug traces behind a feature flag.
Priya Nair: Can we ensure sample rate is configurable per-customer to control telemetry costs for Dedicated/Private deployments?
Ava Chen: Added a config knob telemetry.sample_rate.override per deployment type and documented defaults in the exporter README.
Liam O'Connor: Unit tests look good. Integration tests flaked once on CI (timeout); reran and they passed. Consider increasing test timeout margin for low-RPS environments.
Ava Chen: Increased integration timeout and added a comment explaining flakiness and mitigation.
ci_checks: integration-tests: initially failed (timeout) then rerun: pass
release_notes: Observability: added token-level KV cache tracing and token-level cost/latency dashboards; tuned P95/P99 alerts and added runbook. Notes: metrics have default sampling and aggregation to limit cardinality; operators can configure sampling per deployment.
small_diff_snippets: telemetry/exporter/otlp_token_kv_exporter.py: export span attributes {"kv_key_hash": hash, "cache_hit": bool, "lookup_ms": float} with sampling guard
observability/alerts/token_cost_latency_alerts.yaml: p99_latency_alert: expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_cache_lookup_time_ms_bucket[10s])) by (le, model, deployment)) > 100
notes: Dashboard panels include breakdowns by model, deployment, and route. To reduce cardinality we tag only model_family and deployment_region; route-level detail is sampled via debug flag. Runbook points to incident playbooks and automated mitigations (fallback to smaller model variant, enable KV caching warmup).
testing_and_validation: Load tests were run against a canary pool with long-context prompts (avg 2048 tokens) and showed 18% reduction in observed tail latency after cache warmup; KV miss-rate alert thresholds tuned to reduce noisy pages during rollout. Integration tests validate OTLP export, prom rules, and alert firing in staging.
maintainer_notes: Ops: rollout sequence in README. Default sampling is 1% for production, 10% for staging, and 100% behind debug flag. Private/Dedicated customers can set telemetry.sample_rate.override to 0 to opt-out. Backwards-compatible: proto additions are additive and exporter will ignore unknown fields.
acknowledgements: Thanks to infra/telemetry (Diego), platform (Priya) and SRE (Liam) for review and load validation.
